chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about what Allah has made obligatory of the salat (prayer), so he said: “Five prayers in the night and the day.” I said: “Has Allah named them and clarified them in His Book?” He said: “Yes, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم:”
"Maintain the prayer from the decline of the sun until the darkening of the night."

Its decline means its passing the meridian. So between the decline of the sun and the darkening of the night there are four prayers, which He named, clarified, and timed; and the darkening of the night is its midpoint.
Then He said: “And the recitation of dawn; indeed, the recitation of dawn is witnessed.”
And He said regarding that: “And maintain the prayer at the two ends of the day.”
Its two ends are al-maghrib and al-ghadāh.
"And the early parts of the night."
And it is the prayer of al-ʿishāʾ al-ākhirah.
And He said: “Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer.”

And it is salat al-ẓuhr, and it is the first prayer performed by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It is the middle of the day and between two prayers in the daytime: salat al-ghadāh and salat al-ʿaṣr.
And in some recitation: “Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer, the prayer of al-ʿaṣr, and stand before Allah devoutly obedient.”

He said: “This verse was sent down on the day of Friday while the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was on a journey, so he recited qunūt in it and left it in that state in travel and residence. And he added two rakʿahs for the resident. The two rakʿahs which the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم added on Friday for the resident were only instituted because of the two sermons with the Imam. So whoever performs it on Friday outside congregation should perform it as four rakʿahs like salat al-ẓuhr on the rest of the days.”

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the obligatory salat (prayer) discussed in the hadith
key_terms.الْجُمُعَةِ: Friday, referring to the congregational Friday prayer
key_terms.الْفَجْرِ: dawn, referring to the time of the morning prayer
key_terms.الْوُسْطَىٰ: the middle prayer, explained here as salat al-ẓuhr
key_terms.دُلُوكِ: the sun’s decline from the meridian, marking the beginning of a prayer time
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two units of prayer added for the resident in the Friday prayer context
key_terms.غَسَقِ: the darkening of the night, explained here as its midpoint

ai.seo_question: How does the Qur'an indicate the five daily prayers and what is the ruling of Friday prayer outside congregation?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that Allah obligated five daily prayers and that their times and identities are indicated in the Qur'an. Imam Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام interprets several verses as referring to the daily prayers and also explains the ruling of Jumuʿah prayer for the resident and the one praying outside congregation.
